title: End-to-End Evaluation of Federated Learning and Split Learning for Internet of Things
reasoning: The paper is a technical evaluation of machine learning training methods (Federated Learning and Split Learning) in an Internet of Things (IoT) context. Its focus is on performance metrics like accuracy, convergence speed, communication overhead, and power consumption. It does not engage with topics of religion, faith, spirituality, morals, or ethics. The motivation for the techniques includes data privacy, but this is treated as a technical problem to be solved, not as part of a broader ethical evaluation.
